feature: Scrubbing back fast keeps the picture moving
summary: Dragging the playhead backwards quickly over a screen recording no longer freezes the video picture for half a second: the picture follows the hand, a little softer while it moves, and turns sharp when you hold still.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a full-screen screen recording (the walk uses Scripts/playtest/fixtures/Full screen Retina recording 3456x2234.mp4) and open the timeline.

try.do: Drag the playhead to near the end of the recording and hold it there until the picture is sharp.
Drag it quickly back towards the start without letting go.
Stop moving, still holding the playhead, and watch the picture sharpen.
Drag forward and back across the same stretch a few times, fast and slow.
Let go and press Space to play from there.

evaluate: Does the picture keep moving with your hand the whole way back, with no stretch where it sits still?
Is the softer picture while you drag acceptable, or does it look broken rather than rough?
When you stop, does it turn sharp quickly enough that you never wait for it?
Does playing from where you let go look exactly as it did before?
rough: While the hand moves, the picture is read at most 800 pixels wide, so on a big canvas zoomed in it is visibly soft until you hold still (Premiere and Final Cut do the same while scrubbing).
Holding still for about 30ms counts as stopping; at the far end of a two second stretch the sharp frame took about 230ms to arrive, just inside the quarter second the task asked for.
No surface changed, so there is no mock to compare against: this is how the existing timeline scrub feels, not what it looks like.
